Coagulation: Coagulation is the property of plasma.
Coagulation is the cascade of enzymatic reaction at the end of which soluble fibrinogen is converted into insoluble fibrin.
Normally fibrinogen is soluble in blood, but at end it converts into fibrin strand.

Platelet: Healthy endothelial cells don't allow activated coagulation
Heparan sulphate is present on every endothelial cell.
Anti-thrombin - III can stick on the surface of heparan sulface and activates it.
Thrombomodulin binds with thrombin and modulates the function of thrombin.
It can convert protein Plasminogen coming from liver into plasmin.
Hence healthy endothlial lining is tissue which is anti-coagulant and anti-platelet.
